planned_endpoints.summary: Find employees corresponding with sent data.

rules: ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'NO_ACCESS' (safest default — avoids 422 errors). Only use 'STANDARD' if email login is explicitly needed.
startDate is a TOP-LEVEL field on the employee object. Do NOT put it inside an employments array.
dateOfBirth is a TOP-LEVEL field. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
jobTitle is set via PUT /employee/{id} AFTER creation — it cannot be set in the initial POST.
Do NOT include an 'employments' array in POST /employee — employment details go via separate POST /employee/employment endpoint.

For occupation codes (STYRK/yrkeskode): POST /employee/employment first, then GET /employee/employment/occupationCode?nameAndCode=XXXX to find the code, then PUT /employee/employment/details to set it.

payload.headline: Near-perfect employee onboarding; one check failed, likely wrong salary field in initial POST
what_went_wrong: Initial POST /employee/employment/details used 'salary' field instead of 'annualSalary', causing salary=0 in first creation attempt.
First PUT /employee/employment/details/3750901 used wrong enum values ('FIXED_SALARY', 'NOT_SHIFT_WORK') causing 422 validation error, requiring a second PUT call.
Check 5 failed — likely the employment details POST with wrong 'salary' field left some state issue, or the percentageOfFullTimeEquivalent was set in details rather than only in employment record.
2 wasted API calls (failed PUT + inspect endpoint) added latency and errors, reducing efficiency bonus eligibility.
what_worked: All core entities created correctly: department, employee, employment, standardTime with correct values.
Parallel API calls (e.g., employment type lookups alongside employee creation) reduced total time.
what_to_try_next: Use 'annualSalary' directly in the initial POST /employee/employment/details to avoid the correction PUT call.
Pre-fetch correct enum values via inspect_tripletex_endpoint BEFORE making employment/details calls to avoid 422 errors on wrong enum strings.
Skip the intermediate GET /employee/employment/remunerationType and /workingHoursScheme lookups by using inspect_tripletex_endpoint once upfront to get all enum values needed for employment/details.
unnecessary_calls: GET /employee/employment/remunerationType — enum values could be obtained from inspect_tripletex_endpoint instead
GET /employee/employment/workingHoursScheme — same as above, redundant with schema inspection
First PUT /employee/employment/details/3750901 with wrong enum values — avoidable with upfront schema inspection
